title: One Ångström Inside the 33-Subunit Pyroptotic Barrel — Dinarello Leaderless IL-1β, Shao & Dixit 2015 Gasdermin D Screens, Autoinhibited Human GSDMD (PDB 6N9O) & Electrostatic Sieving Inside the 215 Å Pore (PDB 6VFE)

teenKit.tldr: When your cells detect danger, they trigger a protein called Gasdermin D to punch massive, 33-subunit barrel pores into their own membranes, letting out inflammatory alarms while filtering specific danger molecules like IL-1β.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how these microscopic biological weapons operate inside us could unlock new treatments for runaway fevers, autoimmune disorders, and lethal inflammatory shock.
keyTakeaways: At an Ångström scale, water molecules act like giant, violent boulders smashing into everything due to thermal kinetic energy.
Gasdermin D starts out fully autoinhibited (folded shut), waiting for inflammatory caspases to cleave and activate it.
The final assembled pore forms a massive 215 Å ring that uses electrostatic sieving to selectively release mature IL-1β.

vocab.meaning: A unit of length equal to one ten-billionth of a meter, roughly the diameter of a single hydrogen atom.
A pore-forming effector protein that executes inflammatory cell death (pyroptosis) upon cleavage.
A highly inflammatory form of programmed cell death triggered by infections or cellular damage.
A mechanism where a molecular channel sorts and lets through specific molecules based on their electrical charge.

quiz.question: What happens to gravity and movement when you shrink down to the scale of a single Ångström?
options: Mass-based gravity doubles, making you feel extremely heavy.
Up and down completely disappear, and water molecules act like massive tumbling boulders battering you via Brownian motion.
You float smoothly and effortlessly without any outside forces acting on you.
You fall straight to the bottom of the cell membrane due to standard fluid dynamics.
quiz.explanation: At the microscale, mass-based gravity is irrelevant, and thermal kinetic energy drives chaotic molecular bombardment.

quiz.question: How does Gasdermin D transition from an inactive state to a pore-forming weapon?
options: Inflammatory caspases cleave the protein to release its autoinhibition so it can oligomerize into a barrel pore.
It absorbs heat from the cell until it melts into a circular shape.
It binds directly to DNA to replicate its own channel structure.
Ribosomes continuously pump out pre-assembled rings whenever a fever starts.
quiz.explanation: Proteins like GSDMD are kept autoinhibited until precise enzymatic cleavage by caspases triggers their self-assembly.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of the inner electrostatic features inside the 215 Å Gasdermin D pore?
options: To generate electrical power for the dying cell's mitochondria.
To attract random cellular debris indiscriminately.
To selectively sieve and release specific mature cytokines like IL-1β.
To lock the pore permanently shut so nothing can escape.
quiz.explanation: The pore uses precise electrostatic charges to preferentially filter and release mature signaling molecules like IL-1β.
